messages:
Alex H: FYI customer corp-9876 reported a big p95/p99 regression starting around 09:07 UTC right after the rollout. CS pushed through an escalation (ticket #CS-4892).
Maya S: copied — I see their requests are extremely high-cardinality (many unique prefixes) and we're getting a fanout effect on cold cache. p95 climbed from ~140ms -> 420ms.
Priya R: any obvious errors in the API logs? auth/billing?
Alex H: No 5xxs, just latency spikes and a few 429s from our kv-coordinator. Examples: r=9f3a2c, r=9f3a9b, r=9f3b10.
Tom B: pulled traces for r=9f3a2c — spans show long wait on kv-fetch (~360ms) and repeated misses causing synchronous backfill.
OpsBot: Deploy: rollout-2026-03-17 completed at 09:05 UTC (canary -> global).
Priya R: linking to heatmap: https://redwood-internal/heatmaps/corp-9876/09-07-09-20 — you'll see tail spike aligns with rollout.
Maya S: root cause hypothesis: the recent header-normalize change added X-Client-Tag into the prefix key. That increased key cardinality and broke sticky-hash heuristics -> more cold misses and eviction churn.
Alex H: confirm: the change was in runtime v2.4.3 (PR #4242) which appended client tags to prefix key to improve multi-tenant isolation.
Jen L: we have quick repro on staging: run the following load mix with unique client-tags and compare p95.
Jen L: ```
# repro: simulate fanout
ab -n 10000 -c 50 -H "X-Client-Tag: user-$RANDOM" http://staging.example/api/generate
```
Tom B: reproduction logs (staging): kv-miss-rate rose from 4% -> 38% within ~2 minutes. memstats show LRU churn and eviction count spike.
Priya R: what does current KV config look like?
Maya S: snippet from runtime config (deployed): ```json
{"kv_cache_ttl_s":60,"kv_cache_max_keys":500000,"eviction_policy":"approx_lru","prefix_normalize":"on","include_headers":["X-Client-Tag"]}
```
Alex H: mitigation options: 1) rollback header inclusion (fast) 2) increase cache max_keys temporarily 3) change eviction to segmented LRU / ghost 4) add client-tag canonicalization (hash-bucketize) so we don't create full cardinality keys.
CS Escalation: customer is sensitive to latency; they asked for temporary mitigation ASAP.
Jen L: can we do a hotfix to strip X-Client-Tag from prefix key for corp-9876 as a targeted rule? That would be minimal blast radius.
Tom B: yes we can push a routing rule in the prefix-normalizer: if tenant==corp-9876 then exclude X-Client-Tag. Small config flip and reload (~5min) with no deploy.
Maya S: while we apply that, we should also flip canary back (rollout-2026-03-17 -> rollback header change). OpsBot: started rollback task: rollback-4242 targeting header-normalize change.
OpsBot: Rollback initiated at 09:32 UTC.
Alex H: CS: let customer know we're doing a targeted prefix-normalize override and rolling back the header change; ask if they can test and report p95.
CS Escalation: customer confirmed they see p95 drop to ~160ms after the override. They're happy for now but request root cause analysis and permanent fix.
Priya R: follow-ups: 1) add unit/integration test that simulates high-cardinality header churn and ensures we don't include free-form headers in prefix keys by default. 2) add a config knob to bucketize/tag headers when included. 3) write monitoring that alerts on miss-rate > 10% sustained for 5m per-tenant.
Tom B: also need to audit other headers included by partners (e.g., X-Device-Id). We need a whitelist, not a blacklist.
Maya S: doc the mitigation playbook in runbook: prefix-cold-fanout.md with steps: identify tenant -> add normalizer override -> throttle client-tags -> increase cache-> rollback deploy.
Jen L: I'll open an RFC for canonicalization + segmented LRU proposal. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre for review.
Alex H: great. Thanks all — summary for CS: rollback header change + targeted prefix override applied, customer p95 improved; tracking long-term fixes (bucketize headers, tests, monitoring).
CS Escalation: thanks team :heart:, ticket #CS-4892 updated with mitigation notes.
Maya S: filing follow-up tasks: ENG-RT-1123 (bucketize headers), ENG-SRE-998 (monitor miss-rate), ENG-RT-1124 (whitelist audit).
Tom B: I'll leave logs and the repro harness in the incident folder: /incidents/2026-03-17/cold-fanout.
Alex H: closing thread here unless something else pops up.
